source.title: Deep neural networks have an inbuilt Occam’s razor
source.authors: Chris Mingard; H. Rees; Guillermo Valle-Pérez; A. Louis

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including main text and supplementary notes; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports fully connected networks trained to perfect training accuracy on CIFAR-10 and MNIST, including MNIST with corrupted labels. This is a different architecture and study focus from the version's convolutional-network claim, but it bears on whether gradient-trained networks reach zero training classification error.
record.gate_note: Training accuracy is reported as a stopping condition, not as a comparative outcome. The study says its FCNs were trained until they first reached 100% training accuracy. Generalization-error results and cited prior-work results are not rows. The MNIST corruption percentages are separate reported conditions.
record.test_reason: Figure S10 reports an initialization-dependent training-speed result in a Boolean classification setting: networks initialized with σw=0.5 trained very slowly, leaving some curves incomplete. This bears on V4. R1–R10 concern fully connected networks, outside V1's convolutional-network scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that structured data and an architecture-induced simplicity bias jointly explain first-order generalization, with Bayesian approximations capturing the dominant SGD posterior trends. Perfect training accuracy is a conditioning/stopping criterion, rather than their principal conclusion about optimization.
record.recipe_differences: Fully connected tanh networks rather than convolutional networks; the study focuses on generalization and function bias, and reports perfect training accuracy as the criterion for analyzing generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization weight standard deviation and depth vary in the study's generalization analyses, but the reported training-accuracy stopping outcome remains 100%.

fits_no_version.finding: The analyzed fully connected networks attained 100% training accuracy on CIFAR-10 and MNIST subsets, including corrupted MNIST labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully connected tanh networks can interpolate these image-classification subsets under the reported SGD recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing initialization scale and depth changes function priors and generalization after fitting the training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization-induced simplicity bias affects generalization through its alignment with data structure.

record.problems: Training accuracy is stated as a stopping condition rather than independently summarized by model or condition; the paper does not report failures to reach the criterion or time-to-fit comparisons. CIFAR-10 results use FCNs, not convolutional networks.
record.rows_left_out: Figure S19 also depicts corruption rates 0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 50%, 60%, and 80%; the 0%, 25%, and 50% conditions are already represented from the main Figure 3 caption, and remaining supplementary rates beyond those retained were omitted to avoid duplicate rows for the same reported aggregate stopping outcome.

untested.parts: Training-error outcomes for convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and comparisons involving size, early stopping or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Quantified speed differences, signal/gradient preservation as the cause, maximum trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery and divergence.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, including Fixup.

missing.what: Add the qualitative training-speed result: σw=0.5 was very slow to train, so some Figure S10 curves are incomplete. Record the ten-layer FCNs, Adam, Boolean tasks, activation/loss conditions shown, and the absence of numerical timing or a panel-specific attribution.

record.verdict_notes: The original V1 support verdict should be removed. States of cannot_determine refer to the named claim versions, not to doubt that the analyzed FCNs achieved the stated training accuracy. Generalization degradation with depth or initialization is not evidence of training-error degradation.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests fully connected networks, not convolutional networks; it reports CIFAR-10 but not CIFAR-100; and its label corruption experiments are on MNIST rather than random labels on CIFAR.
